note: Per-town landmark rules for historicize_town.py (year 1650). 'keep': OSM building names (exact, or substring when the entry ends with '*') that existed by 1650: always kept, marked with lm = kind and given display name 'as' if set. Kinds: church, belfry, townhall, clothhall, beguinage, castle, abbey, hall (guild/meat hall), gate, tower, house. 'drop': name substrings of buildings known to be later than 1650 (removed even when Ferraris shows the plot built up, since their footprint is not a 1650 one). 'pois': extra points (town-local metres) for things that are areas rather than one building. A keep entry may name an OSM way id instead ('id'), for unnamed buildings.

landmarks.y1650: Gothic collegiate church. A fire in 1458 destroyed the old tower front; Joost Metsys became master of the new west towers about 1505 (stone model 1524-30), a three-tower front meant to be among the highest in Christendom, never finished: in 1650 the stumps stood. Whether the soft ground was the reason is NOT verified here.

landmarks.n: Belfort met Klokke Roeland en de draak
landmarks.y1650: Belfry begun before 1313, four of six storeys done by 1323; a provisional wooden crown of 1377-80 carried the gilded copper dragon weathervane made in 1377 (replaced only in 1853). Klokke Roeland, cast 1314, still hung in it in 1650: Pieter Hemony melted it down in 1659 for the new carillon. Sanderus says the dragon was made to spit fire at feasts. The town charters were kept in the 'secreet' inside.
landmarks.footprintNote: 91 m is today's height with the 1913 spire; the 1650 wooden crown was lower (not verified)

landmarks.y1650: Cloth hall built 1425-45 against the belfry, left unfinished; used by the fencers' guild of Sint-Michiel since 1613.
Cathedral since 1559 (formerly Sint-Jans); west tower finished 1534 (89 m), holds the Ghent Altarpiece of the Van Eycks.
Scheldt-Gothic church of the merchants on the Korenmarkt; its crossing tower served as the town's first belfry.
Wrought-iron 15th-c. bombard of about 12,500 kg, on the Groentenmarkt by the Lieve since 1578.
Castle of the counts of Flanders (1180); in 1650 used as court of the Council of Flanders, prison and mint, built over with houses.
Citadel built 1540-45 for Charles V on the site of the Sint-Baafsabdij, garrison of c. 2500; Egmont and Horne were held here 1567-68.
Town hall: late-Gothic wing of 1518-60 (unfinished) and Renaissance wing of 1595-1618.
Gothic church whose great tower was never finished.
Beguinage of Our Lady ter Hooie (founded 1234), on its present site.
The great beguinage then stood west of the Gravensteen at Sint-Elisabeth (moved to Sint-Amandsberg in 1874); its church survives.
Meat hall of 1406-10 on the Groentenmarkt.
Fortified sluice gate on the Lieve, 1489.
Benedictine abbey on the Blandijnberg, rebuilt after the iconoclasm (abbey church 1629-1720 under construction in 1650).
Cloth hall (14th c.) with belfry on the Grote Markt, together with the meat hall; on the UNESCO list of belfries. The Grote Markt was the forecourt of the counts' castle.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Dendermonde' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140019); UNESCO 'Belfries of Belgium and France'

landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Dendermonde' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140019)

landmarks.y1650: Aldermen's house of c. 1225, oldest in the Low Countries, with its belfry tower of 1460; on the UNESCO list of belfries.

landmarks.y1650: Collegiate church begun c. 1480 to a vast plan and never finished: no nave or tower beyond the transept (Rubens's altarpiece of St Roch hangs here from 1623-26).
Beguinage founded 1261.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Aalst' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140017)

landmarks.y1650: Printer Dirk Martens (d. 1534) printed the first book in the Low Countries here in 1473; a statue is 19th c.

Gothic town hall (1401-55) on the Grote Markt; its 96 m tower by Jan van Ruysbroeck carries the gilded Saint Michael slaying the dragon (1455). The Grote Markt's guild houses of 1650 were destroyed in the French bombardment of 1695.
landmarks.special: Saint Michael and the dragon; main bell tower

landmarks.y1650: Ducal bread hall, rebuilt 1504-36 (Keldermans); the present building is a reconstruction of 1873-95 on the same plot.
Collegiate church of Saints Michael and Gudula (Gothic, towers finished 1485); a cathedral only since 1962.
Palace of the dukes of Brabant on the Coudenberg, court of the governor Leopold Wilhelm in 1650; burnt in 1731 (site under today's Koningsplein).
Romanesque-Gothic church of the Marollen; Pieter Bruegel the Elder is buried here (1569).

landmarks.y1650: Bronze fountain figure by Jérôme Duquesnoy the Elder, 1619.
Gate of the second wall (1381), used as a prison; the only surviving gate.
Tower of the first wall (13th c.).
Tower of the first wall.

Cloth hall with the belfry on the Markt; the octagonal top dates from 1482-86 and carried a wooden spire until the fire of 1741, so in 1650 the tower was taller than today's 83 m (spire height not verified).
Gothic town hall on the Burg, 1376-1420.
The cathedral of Bruges (bishopric 1559) stood on the Burg opposite the town hall; demolished from 1799. Position approximate.
Double chapel on the Burg holding the relic of the Holy Blood (procession since the 13th c.).
Church with the brick tower of about 115 m; Michelangelo's Madonna (1504) inside.
Collegiate church of Sint-Salvator (cathedral only from 1834).

Town palace of the lords of Gruuthuse.
Medieval hospital (12th c.).
Belfry on the Grote Markt (14th c.), once part of the cloth hall; on the UNESCO list.
Main parish church, its tower the town's main bell tower.
Collegiate church by the counts' castle; Van Dyck's Raising of the Cross (1631) hangs here. The golden spurs of 1302 hung here until the French took them in 1382.
Two towers guarding the Leie bridge (1385 and 1411-13).
Pentagonal citadel built by the French in 1646-48 on the east flank of Overbeke, held by Spain from 1648, razed 1684; position approximate.

Scheldt-Gothic church across the river (1234).

Cathedral of the bishopric of Ypres (1559-1801); Bishop Cornelius Jansenius (d. 1638) is buried here.
Parish church in the south of the town.
